items.prompt: For generating combinations without reusing earlier indices, which state is essential?

options.text: The next candidate start index.
Only the length of the global result list.
A boolean saying whether the input is sorted.
The total number of recursive calls made so far.

feedback.reason: A start boundary records which candidate indices remain legal for the current combination.

blocks.text: The boundary identifies legal suffix candidates

If the current combination chose index i, the next call starts at i + 1. Restricting candidates to that suffix prevents index reuse and avoids producing the same unordered selection in different orders.

The path stores what has been selected, but equal path lengths can end at different indices and therefore have different legal suffixes. Result count, a sorted flag, and call count do not recover that boundary.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: For order-independent selections without reuse, carry the first still-eligible index.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.last_output_length: Completed-output count is global history and says nothing about which indices this partial combination may choose next.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sorted_flag: Sorting can support duplicate handling, but a boolean flag does not identify the remaining candidate suffix.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recursion_count: Call count measures execution history; two calls with the same count can have different paths and legal candidates.

items.prompt: For generating permutations of n distinct values, which state prevents reusing the same input position within one path?

options.text: A used-by-index set, boolean array, or bitmask.
Only a monotonically increasing start index.
Only the number of completed permutations.
Only the previously chosen value.

feedback.reason: Permutation state must distinguish every input position already selected in the current branch.

blocks.text: Permutations need arbitrary availability

At each output position, any input index not already on the current path may be chosen. A boolean array, set, or n-bit mask answers that membership question and can be updated and restored with each choice.

A monotonically increasing start index would forbid valid orders such as choosing index 2 and then index 0, reducing permutations to combinations. One previous value or a global result count cannot encode all used positions.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: When choice order matters, track membership of every reusable candidate domain position rather than a forward-only boundary.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.start_only: A forward-only boundary prevents choosing a lower index later and therefore omits valid permutation orders.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.result_count: The number of finished permutations is shared across branches and cannot identify availability in the current path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.previous_value: Knowing only the last value leaves all earlier selections unknown, so a previously used position can be chosen again.

items.prompt: A target-sum backtracking solver uses only positive candidate values. Which state can avoid recomputing the sum of the current path?

options.text: The remaining target after chosen values are subtracted.
The maximum input value.
Only recursion depth.
The number of solutions already found.

feedback.reason: Remaining target is a sufficient summary of the path sum for this constraint.

blocks.text: Summarize additive progress
Initialize `remainingTarget = target`. Choosing value x creates child state `remainingTarget - x`; zero means the chosen path reaches the target exactly.

Because every candidate is positive, a negative remainder cannot return to zero, so it is a sound failure condition. Depth alone is insufficient because different values chosen at the same depth produce different sums.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: For an additive target, carry either the current total or the remainder as one canonical summary, not both.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.global_max: The largest candidate is fixed input information and does not reveal how much this branch has accumulated.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.call_depth_only: Paths of equal depth can choose different positive values and therefore have different remaining sums.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.result_size: The number of completed solutions is global output metadata and does not determine whether this branch can reach the target.

items.prompt: A grid word-search call is represented by (row, col, wordIndex). What additional branch-local state is required when cells cannot be reused in the same path?

options.text: Which cells are already used by the current path.
The number of words found in earlier searches.
The sum of values in the current row.
Only the grid dimensions.

feedback.reason: The call coordinates and target position do not encode which cells were used earlier in the branch.

blocks.text: Coordinates do not encode path history

Two calls can be at the same `(row, col, wordIndex)` after different routes. A neighboring cell may be legal in one route and already used in the other, so those three scalars do not fully determine the next moves.

Store the current path's visited cells in a set or matrix, or encode them by reversible board marking. Restore the mark before a sibling so visited means “used by this candidate path,” not globally unavailable.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: If legality depends on the route, state must include a route summary in addition to the current location.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.global_result_count: Earlier outputs do not reveal which cells the current candidate path has used.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.row_sum: A row aggregate loses cell identity and cannot answer whether a specific neighbor is already on the path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.board_size_only: Dimensions support bounds checks, but every route through the same board shares them and can have different used cells.

items.prompt: A k-combination solver also requires the selected values to reach a target sum. Which state is redundant when current path length can be read in O(1)?

options.text: A separate chosenCount field always equal to path.length.
The next legal candidate boundary.
The selected values.
The unresolved target for a constrained-sum problem.

feedback.reason: State that is exactly and cheaply derivable need not be duplicated.

blocks.text: Do not duplicate an exact derived value

`chosenCount` and `path.length` represent the same quantity. If both are mutable, every choose and undo must update both correctly; one missed update makes completion checks disagree with the actual path.

The path holds the candidate output, the start index identifies legal future indices, and remaining target summarizes the independent sum constraint. Those facts are not determined by path length alone.

blocks.title: Minimal-state rule
blocks.text: Keep one canonical owner for each fact; derive cheap views instead of synchronizing duplicate fields.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.start_index: Equal-length paths can end at different indices and therefore have different legal candidate suffixes.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.current_path: The selected values are the partial output itself and cannot be reconstructed from its length.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.remaining_target: The same number of selections can produce different sums, so path length does not determine the unresolved target.

items.prompt: A solver mutates one shared current path. Where should that path belong conceptually?

options.text: Branch-local state whose contents are restored before sibling exploration.
Immutable global configuration shared without restoration.
Only metadata about completed results.
The fixed list of all possible input candidates.

feedback.reason: The current path is mutable state describing the active root-to-node branch.

blocks.text: Physical sharing does not change logical ownership

The path describes exactly the choices on the active root-to-current-node route. A child appends its choice; after that child returns, undo must restore the parent's path before the next sibling runs.

One mutable list can be reused for efficiency, but its contents remain logically branch-local. Immutable candidate input and fixed constraints may be shared without restoration because branches never change them.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Classify state by whether its value changes with the active branch, not by whether one object instance is physically shared.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.global_configuration: Every choice changes the path, so treating it as immutable shared configuration would leak one branch into another.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.result_metadata: The path is the candidate currently being constructed, not a statistic about already completed results.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.candidate_catalog: The catalog contains all possible input choices; the path contains only choices selected by the active branch.

items.prompt: A partitioning solver receives a string and a start index. Which state is sufficient to identify the unresolved suffix?

options.text: The exclusive boundary where the next segment must begin.
Every previous boundary even when the current path already stores the segments.
The number of partitions already found.
Only the final character of the previous segment.

feedback.reason: The next unprocessed position determines the remaining suffix.

blocks.text: One boundary identifies the unresolved suffix
Maintain the invariant that path segments cover exactly [0, start). Then the unresolved input is `string[start:]`, and every next segment must begin at `start` and choose an end after it.

The path already preserves chosen segments for output. Earlier boundaries are unnecessary for locating the next suffix, while result count and the previous segment's final character lose the required position.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: For left-to-right partitioning, carry the first unprocessed index and let the path own output history.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_previous_end_indices: The current start already locates the suffix, and the path retains prior segments, so a second boundary history duplicates information.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.result_count: The number of completed partitions is unrelated to the current branch's first uncovered character.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.last_character_only: The same character can occur at many positions, so its value does not identify where the remaining input begins.

items.prompt: Why is storing the entire remaining substring often less attractive than storing its start index?

options.text: It can create repeated substring copies while the index already identifies the same suffix.
Indices cannot identify positions in a string.
Substring values have no length.
Recursion always requires a copied input.

feedback.reason: A compact boundary can identify the unresolved region without duplicating immutable input data.

blocks.text: Share immutable data and pass a boundary
The pair `(originalString, start)` uniquely identifies the same suffix as a copied substring. Advancing the boundary is O(1) state and lets every call share the original immutable characters.

In runtimes where slicing copies characters, materializing a suffix at every node adds repeated time and memory. A slice view can avoid copying but may retain a large backing string; that is a representation-specific tradeoff, not a reason indices are invalid.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Prefer compact coordinates into shared immutable input when they identify the same unresolved region unambiguously.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.indices_invalid: An index precisely identifies a position when paired with the original string and is the standard suffix boundary representation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.substrings_no_length: Substring values have lengths; the concern is repeated materialization or backing-storage retention, not missing metadata.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recursion_requires_copy: Recursive calls can safely share immutable input and receive only their own scalar boundary.

items.prompt: A solver stores both remainingTarget and the full current sum, updating both independently. What risk does this introduce?

options.text: The two redundant values can become inconsistent after an update or undo.
The branch will be pruned automatically.
Every result is necessarily duplicated.
The algorithm becomes O(1) space.

feedback.reason: Redundant mutable state increases synchronization obligations.

blocks.text: Two equations for one fact can drift

If `remainingTarget = target - currentSum`, choosing x must subtract x from the remainder and add x to the sum; undo must reverse both. Missing any one update breaks the invariant and can cause false completion or pruning.
Keep one canonical mutable value and derive the other when needed, unless profiling proves a real cost that justifies the additional synchronization proof.

blocks.title: Canonical-state rule
blocks.text: When two fields are algebraically equivalent, choose one owner and treat the other as a derived view.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.automatic_pruning: A field enables pruning only when code applies a proved feasibility rule; redundancy alone does nothing automatically.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.duplicate_results: Inconsistent state can cause many defects, but duplicate output is not inevitable and is not the defining risk.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.constant_space: Adding mutable fields increases per-call or shared state and does not remove the recursion stack.

items.prompt: Which fields can form sufficient state for k-combination generation from an indexed array? Select all that apply.

options.text: The next candidate start index.
The values or indices selected so far.
The number of values still required, when not derived from path length.
The total number of calls made across the entire search.

feedback.reason: Sufficient state must identify the partial output, legal candidate range, and remaining completion requirement.

blocks.text: Account for each semantic question

The path answers what has been selected; the start index answers which indices remain legal; the fixed k or a canonical remaining-slots value answers when the selection is complete and whether enough candidates remain.
When path length is O(1), remaining slots can be derived as `k - path.length`; storing both is optional rather than necessary. Global call count is instrumentation and cannot affect legal completion.

blocks.title: Sufficiency test
blocks.text: A call must answer completion and legal-next-choice queries from its state plus immutable configuration.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.global_call_count: Execution count neither identifies the partial combination nor changes which candidate indices can complete it.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.start_index: It identifies the candidate suffix and prevents reuse or reversed duplicate orderings.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.current_path: It is the partial combination that will be copied at completion.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.remaining_slots: As a canonical field or derived value, it supports exact-size completion and remaining-capacity pruning.

items.prompt: Which information can be represented by a used bitmask in a permutation solver? Select all that apply.

options.text: Which input positions are already selected in the current path.
Which positions remain available, by complementing within the n-bit domain.
How many positions are selected, by counting set bits.
The exact order in which selected values appear in the path.

feedback.reason: A bitmask compactly represents membership, but not the ordered path itself.

blocks.text: A mask stores membership, not sequence
Bit i equals one exactly when input position i is used. Masking its n-bit complement yields available positions, and popcount yields how many positions are selected.

The same mask represents every ordering of the same selected positions, so it cannot reconstruct the permutation prefix. Keep an ordered path or an equivalent parent-decision history for output order.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Use masks for finite-domain membership and separate state for any order that affects the result.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.selected_order: Positions chosen as 1 then 3 and as 3 then 1 produce the same mask, so order is lost.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.used_positions: Each of the n bits records membership of one input position.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.available_positions: Within the n-bit domain, complementing used membership gives availability.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.chosen_count: Counting set bits derives the selected-position count without another field.

items.prompt: Which state components are relevant for path-based grid search? Select all that apply.

options.text: The current row and column.
The index or amount of target already matched.
Cells already used in the current path.
The number of unrelated paths found earlier.

feedback.reason: Grid-search state combines location, target progress, and branch-local reuse constraints.

blocks.text: Three independent branch facts
Coordinates identify where the branch is, target progress identifies which symbol must match now, and path-visited state determines whether that cell and its neighbors are reusable in this candidate.
Removing any one merges states with different legal continuations. The count of completed paths is global history and cannot answer any of those branch-local questions.

blocks.title: Sufficiency test
blocks.text: State must distinguish calls whenever their next required symbol or legal neighbors differ.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.completed_result_count: Earlier successes do not identify this call's cell, next target symbol, or used-cell restrictions.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.current_cell: Row and column identify the board value and neighbor coordinates under consideration.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.target_progress: Progress identifies the exact target symbol the current cell must satisfy.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.path_visited: Path-local membership enforces the no-reuse constraint for this candidate.

items.prompt: Which properties suggest that a state field is redundant? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is deterministically and cheaply derived from other state.
It always changes in lockstep with another field and is exactly derivable from that field.
No completion, legality, pruning, or output logic reads it.
It is the only field that determines whether a candidate is legal.

feedback.reason: State should be minimal but sufficient.

blocks.text: Redundancy versus necessity
A cheaply derived field duplicates a fact; a field always synchronized with and derivable from another creates drift risk; a never-read field has no semantic effect. Each is a removal candidate.
By contrast, the only field that answers candidate legality is necessary unless an equivalent representation replaces it. Minimality must not make state insufficient.

blocks.title: Deletion test
blocks.text: Remove a field only if every completion, legality, pruning, update, and output query remains answerable.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.branch_legality: If no other state can decide whether a candidate is legal, removing the field merges semantically different nodes.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.cheaply_derivable: A cheap deterministic derivation keeps one canonical owner and avoids synchronization.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.must_sync_on_undo: Exact derivability plus lockstep mutation adds an unnecessary opportunity for choose/undo drift.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.never_read: A field unused by every semantic decision or output has no effect on behavior.

items.prompt: Which state should normally be immutable configuration shared by all branches? Select all that apply.

options.text: The original candidate list when branches do not modify it.
The fixed target or constraint definition.
The mutable selected path.
The current path's visited-cell set.

feedback.reason: Shared immutable configuration is distinct from mutable branch state.

blocks.text: Separate configuration from branch state
The original candidates and fixed target or constraints have the same value for every node, so branches can safely share them as immutable configuration.
The current path and visited set change with choices. They must be copied per child or mutated and restored before siblings; treating them as immutable shared data leaks one branch into another.

blocks.title: Ownership rule
blocks.text: Share facts that never change; isolate or restore facts whose value depends on the active root-to-node path.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.current_path: Each branch selects different values, so the path must be isolated or restored between siblings.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.path_visited: Used-cell membership depends on the current route and cannot be one immutable set shared by all routes.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.input_candidates: When branches do not mutate it, every call can read one candidate list safely.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.target_contract: The fixed target and constraint definition govern every branch without changing.

items.prompt: Arrange the process for designing backtracking state.

elements.text: Define what a complete valid result means.
Define which next choices are legal from a partial state.
Choose the minimal fields needed to answer completion and legality questions.
Specify how every field changes and is restored for one branch.

feedback.reason: State design follows from the result and transition contracts.

blocks.text: Derive fields from semantic queries
Completion defines what the state must prove at a leaf. Legality defines which facts distinguish the possible children. Only then can fields be selected to answer those queries without duplication.
Finally specify choose and undo for every mutable field; otherwise the declared state invariant may hold for the child but not be restored for its siblings.

items: Define each field's child update and exact restoration.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Do not invent fields first; derive them from the questions each recursive call must answer.

items.prompt: Arrange the state update for a target-sum branch using remainingTarget.
constraints: remainingTarget is mutable branch state updated in place.

elements.text: Verify that the candidate is legal for the current state.
Subtract the chosen value from remainingTarget.
Add the value back when returning to the parent state.

feedback.reason: The child state must reflect the choice, and the parent state must be restored afterward.

blocks.text: Preserve the remainder invariant
Maintain `remainingTarget = target - sum(path)`. After confirming candidate x is legal, subtracting x makes the invariant true for the child path that includes x.

After recursion, add x back so the next sibling sees the parent's original remainder. Restoring before recursion would erase the choice; omitting restoration would accumulate values from unrelated siblings.

items: Check x against the parent state.
Subtract x to create the child remainder.
Add x back to restore the parent.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Every in-place choose update needs an inverse undo after the child returns.

items.prompt: A permutation solver stores a length-n boolean used array and a recursion path of depth at most n, excluding materialized outputs. Select the auxiliary-space complexity.
constraints: Only one depth-first branch is active at a time.

feedback.reason: The used array and active recursion path each scale linearly with n.

blocks.text: Add simultaneous auxiliary structures
The boolean used array stores n entries. The mutable permutation path holds at most n values, and the active call stack has at most n frames.
These structures coexist, so their space is O(n) + O(n) + O(n) = O(n). Factorially many materialized permutations are excluded by the prompt; total search work does not become simultaneous memory.

blocks.title: Space rule
blocks.text: Sum structures live at the same time; do not multiply them by the number of sequentially explored branches.

items.prompt: A grid search solver uses an R by C auxiliary visited matrix and an independent recursion-depth cap L. Select its auxiliary-space bound, excluding the immutable grid.
constraints: The visited matrix is stored explicitly.
At most L recursive calls are active.
No asymptotic relation between L and RC is assumed.

feedback.reason: Explicit visited state and the active recursion stack contribute separate terms.

blocks.text: Keep independent parameter terms
The explicit matrix contains R · C entries, giving O(RC). At most L call frames coexist, giving O(L) stack space.

Because the prompt declares no relation between the parameters, neither term absorbs the other, so auxiliary space is O(RC + L). Reversible in-place board marking could remove the matrix term, but that is a different representation.

blocks.title: Space rule
blocks.text: For independent dimensions, retain additive terms unless the contract proves one asymptotically dominates.
